CweFindings.Name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
CweFindings.Description: The product does not properly check inputs that are used for loop conditions, potentially leading to a denial of service or other consequences because of excessive looping.
CweFindings.Explanation: IndexModel.OnPostUploadAsync iterates over the caller-provided files collection without enforcing the configured MaxFilesPerUpload value. The number of per-file service operations is therefore controlled by the submitted multipart request; the request body has an overall limit but the individual loop count is not checked against the application limit.

CweFindings.Name: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
CweFindings.Description: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.
CweFindings.Explanation: PhotoService.UploadPhotoAsync passes a newly opened IFormFile stream directly to Image.LoadAsync without disposing the stream. The subsequent OpenReadStream call at line 132 is also not disposed, leaving request stream wrappers unreleased after dimension extraction.

CweFindings.Name: Use of Hard-coded Password
CweFindings.Description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.
CweFindings.Explanation: The infrastructure template defines the SQL administrator password inline as a deterministic value derived from deployment identifiers and supplies it to the SQL server module. This embeds password construction in source rather than accepting a secret from a protected provisioning input.

CweFindings.Name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
CweFindings.Description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
CweFindings.Explanation: The infrastructure template embeds construction of the SQL administrator credential in source and passes that value to the SQL server module, making a credential part of the deployed infrastructure definition.

CweFindings.Name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
CweFindings.Description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.
CweFindings.Explanation: PhotoService.UploadPhotoAsync accepts uploads based on the client-supplied ContentType allowlist, preserves the extension from the user-supplied filename, and writes bytes under the static web root. ImageSharp load failure is caught and upload continues, so content is not required to be a valid image. Program enables static file serving for the upload directory, allowing mismatched or active content with a permitted claimed MIME type to be stored and publicly served.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
CweFindings.Description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
CweFindings.Explanation: PhotoService.UploadPhotoAsync trusts the client-supplied MIME type, preserves the uploaded filename extension, and continues after ImageSharp fails to decode the content. The file is saved below wwwroot, and Program enables static-file serving there. An attacker can upload HTML bytes while claiming an allowed image MIME type and using an .html extension; the static-file middleware can serve the uploaded content as an active same-origin HTML page.
